$note: LAYER 3. Product concepts with fixed visual contracts, defined ONCE so they cannot drift between screens. References semantic tokens only — never primitives. Several families exist as reserved slots for screens that are not designed yet; that is deliberate, so building those screens does not reopen the token layer.

$negativeSpace.$note: What is deliberately ABSENT here is as load-bearing as what is present. These names must never be added, and restricted.mjs fails the build if they are: corridor.target / corridor.goal (a corridor is a range, never a line you can fall short of); streak.* / chain.* / broken.* (nothing may visually break); missed.* (a gap is rest, not failure). The principle is enforced by the shape of the token set, not by review.

corridor.$intent: Answer 'am I on track?' without letting anyone fail a benchmark nobody told them about.
corridor.$contract: A soft translucent band behind the chart, labelled as a common range, with phase chips describing what typically happens and an 'everyone heals differently' affordance always within reach.

band.$description: The range band itself. Sits UNDER the data line; the data must always read on top. The chart previously painted a different base on dark (accent.strong at 12.9%) — the rendered results differ by 3 RGB units, which is why the token's simpler mode-invariant form was kept rather than the code's.

edge.$description: The dashed boundaries. RAISED from 20% to 27% to match what the chart actually painted, because the CODE was right about this one: the two dashes are what make the band read as a range with two sides rather than as a threshold you are above or below. That is N5 doing real work, and the weaker token would have quietly undermined it. Still under the 3:1 non-text floor and declared decorative — the band fill and the 'common range for …' label both carry the meaning independently.

label.$description: "Common range for …" — deliberately quiet. The band is context, not a verdict.

rest.$intent: Render gaps as rest. Missing days are the normal texture of recovery, not a failure state.
rest.$contract: Muted neutral, visually quieter than a logged day. Never red, never alert-coloured, never labelled 'missed', never counted.

label.$description: Copy reads like "a few quiet days" — descriptive, never evaluative.

accumulation.$intent: Show consistency without a chain that can break. Research puts guilt among the top abandonment drivers, and a broken streak manufactures it.
accumulation.$contract: A count, or dots that only ever accrue. Nothing sequential that can visibly reset.

dotEmpty.$description: An unfilled dot is neutral, not a hole. It never turns red and never carries a count of what was skipped.

lock.$contract: Measured from Figma node 2:560, the only frame carrying this treatment. One badge, one desaturation level, one behaviour: tapping opens the paywall sheet.
lock.$forbiddenOn: Any core-loop surface, and the entire doctor report including its export. Free forever means no badge, ever.

cardOpacity.$description: Row desaturation. From Figma — the code had it inline.

label.$description: Locked rows demote their label from primary to secondary — the row reads as available-later, not as broken.

historyFade.$intent: Gate history depth without hiding that the data exists.
historyFade.$contract: A gradient fade at the free-history boundary plus an inline unlock pill. Never a hard wall, never a modal interrupt.

insight.$intent: Make data mean something. Charts without interpretation are a top-cited reason people quit.
insight.$contract: The headline sentence is the primary element and the chart supports it. Trend is icon PLUS word — never a bare colour or arrow.

trendUp.$description: INK, not mark. These roles colour a WORD ("Improving"), which is text, and mark fails as text on light — 1.47-1.96:1. They pointed at mark until the RN port tried to consume them, which would have reintroduced the exact defect the web prototype had just been cleaned of.

trendDown.$description: INK, not mark — see trendUp. Direction is not valence: falling pain is good. The WORD carries the meaning; colour only supports it, which is also why this must never be the reserved safety hue.

fastPath.$intent: The core retention mechanic: a complete, valid check-in in one tap, under ten seconds, without typing.
fastPath.$contract: Largest and first-rendered element on its screen, in the thumb zone. Each option is icon plus word. No scroll, no second decision.
fastPath.$wasContradictory: This family defined BOTH a single `optionSelected` (accent at 27%) AND per-option marks for better/same/worse. Those cannot both describe the selected state, and the contrast manifest settles it: the five `category ink on 27% tint` pairs exist because the fast path fills its selected option with a tint of that option's OWN mark, and five pastelInk values were re-solved against exactly those backdrops. A uniform accent fill would strand that calibration and duplicate `state.selectedFill` at a different alpha, which semantic.json warns against by name. `optionSelected` was the vestigial half and is gone.
fastPath.$wasMissing: There was no `ink`. The screen renders the selected WORD in the category ink — correctly — and the family had no role that could say so, which is how a family stays dormant while the screen quietly does the right thing by hand.

optionFill.$description: NOT surface.raised, which is what the screen painted. On surface.base, card lifts further — and this is the one control that should be unmissable on a bad day. Adopting it is also what exposed the dark-mode failure recorded on pastelInk.painOnDark.

minHeight.$description: Twice the 44pt floor. This is the one control that should be unmissable on a bad day.

share.$intent: Milestone artifacts people choose to send. The honest growth loop.
share.$contract: Dignified, story-friendly ratio, light brandmark, MODE-INVARIANT. STRICTLY user-initiated — no share prompts anywhere.
share.$status: RESERVED — ShareCardScreen exists in code but has no Figma frame, and still has no dev route or baseline. MilestoneDetail is the first surface to consume this family.
share.$bug: This family carried the SAME defect as dayCard, and it was never fixed because nothing consumed it. `cardFrom` referenced {color.accent.dim} — mode-invariant, a deep indigo — while `title` referenced {color.text.primary}, which flips to near-black in light. Light mode therefore put #1A1830 on #3D3668: 1.58:1, the identical figure §11 records as the worst contrast in the system. accent.dim's own note already said 'NOT safe behind secondary text'. It survived because ShareCardScreen hardcodes #fff and never rendered these tokens — the Toast situation exactly: the screen was right and the family was wrong.
share.$why: The resolution is NOT dayCard's, though. A share card is an ARTIFACT that leaves the app: the recipient never sees the sender's colour mode, so a card that changes with it is inventing a variable the medium does not have. The screen always drew one dark card in both modes, and the tokens now say what it always did — the same reasoning that made the Toast mode-invariant.

cardFrom.$description: Mode-invariant BY DECISION. Was {color.accent.dim}, which resolves to the same hex but implied it should track the accent.

cardTo.$description: Mode-invariant. Was {color.surface.raised}, which flipped to white in light and gave the title nothing to sit on.

meta.$description: 5.01 on cardFrom, 7.59 on cardTo. Was {color.text.secondary}, which reached 3.90 at the gradient START even in dark — a failure that existed on BOTH sides and was declared on neither.

brandmark.$description: Light touch. The user's milestone is the subject; the app is a footnote.

report.$intent: The doctor report — the spec flagship and the category's emotional peak.
report.$contract: Restrained, print-friendly, scannable by a clinician in 60 seconds. 'What changed since last visit' is the visually dominant block.
report.$status: RESERVED — exists in NEITHER Figma nor code, despite being linked from both Home and Profile. Recorded as a product risk in extraction/screens.json.
report.$never: No lock badge, no paywall, no premium treatment anywhere on this surface or its export. Free forever.

changeBlock.$description: The 'what changed' block — the one section allowed extra visual weight.

welcomeBack.$intent: Meet a returning user with warmth, never a recap of what they missed.
welcomeBack.$contract: One warm line, then straight into the fast path. No count of missed days, no catch-up prompt, no apology required.
welcomeBack.$status: RESERVED — no design in either source.

paywall.$intent: Offer depth without ever compromising the free experience.
paywall.$contract: A dismissible bottom sheet. Dismissing always returns to a fully intact free product.
paywall.$never: Countdown timers, fake urgency, guilt copy, or a skip path that is hidden, delayed or visually starved.

savingsLabel.$description: INK, not mark. This referenced {color.category.mood.mark} — a FILL — and used it as text: 1.58:1 against the sheet in light, and 1.45:1 on its own savings tint. The same mark-as-text mistake InsightSentence made, and the same figure as the dayCard and share.* bugs. It survived because the SCREEN already drew mood.ink; the defect lived entirely in a definition nothing rendered. Found by checks/consumption.mjs, which exists because this had already happened three times.

capture.$intent: The Notes-app lane: capture anything in under ten seconds with zero categorisation decisions.
capture.$contract: One line, one save. No required fields, ever. Offline-safe and optimistic — the entry appears immediately and the write is never something the user waits on.

dayCard.$intent: The Day-N counter card — the product's emotional anchor and the first thing a returning user looks at.
dayCard.$contract: A gradient card carrying the day count, condition, start date and a week-over-week comparison. Text must stay legible across the WHOLE gradient, not just at the end where it happens to be lightest.
dayCard.$bug: The light mode of this card reused the DARK gradient's start (accent.dim, a deep indigo) while keeping near-black text, giving 1.58:1 at the top of the card — the worst contrast in the entire system, and worse than anything in the original audit. It went unnoticed because the contrast manifest only declared pairs against FLAT surfaces; a gradient needs BOTH endpoints declared as backdrops. Light now mirrors dark properly: dark goes deep-to-darker with light text, light goes pale-to-white with dark text.

from.$description: Both modes are constrained by SECONDARY text at this stop, not primary — the numeral is comfortable either way. Dark needed deepening from accent.dim (3.90:1) and light needed the palest lavender that still works (4.54:1).

primary.$description: The Day-N numeral. Clears 9.60 dark / 14.96 light at the gradient start.

secondary.$description: Condition and start date. Clears 4.54 light at the gradient start — the constraint that set paper.100.

toast.$contract: A dark pill in BOTH modes, floating above the shell, pointer-events none, gone in 2.4s. Never blocks, never requires dismissal, never reports a failure — the capture path cannot fail, so there is nothing for a toast to apologise for.
toast.$note:
surface/label were originally surface.card and text.primary — mode-paired, so light mode would have rendered a WHITE pill with dark text. The screen never did that; it forced the dark value with a hardcoded mode argument, and the mismatch went unnoticed because the token family was consumed by nothing.

The SCREEN was right and the tokens were wrong. An always-dark confirmation pill is the platform snackbar convention, and the reason is sound: on a light screen a dark pill reads as system chrome rather than as part of the page, which is what makes a two-second message noticeable without shouting. So the tokens now say what the product always did, via surface.notification.

Worth being precise about what was NOT wrong here: contrast. The pill renders 15.13:1 either way. This was dead code and a token family describing a design nobody had built — not an accessibility defect.
